title: K Concatenation Maximum Sum
description:
Given an integer array arr and an integer k, modify the array by repeating it k times.
For example, if arr = [1, 2] and k = 3 then the modified array will be [1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2].
Return the maximum sub-array sum in the modified array. Note that the length of the sub-array can be 0 and its sum in that case is 0.
As the answer can be very large, return the answer modulo 109 + 7.
 
Example 1:

Input: arr = [1,2], k = 3
Output: 9

Example 2:

Input: arr = [1,-2,1], k = 5
Output: 2

Example 3:

Input: arr = [-1,-2], k = 7
Output: 0

 
Constraints:

1 <= arr.length <= 105
1 <= k <= 105
-104 <= arr[i] <= 104

def check(candidate):
    assert candidate(arr = [1, 2],k = 3) == 9
    assert candidate(arr = [1, -2, 1],k = 5) == 2
    assert candidate(arr = [-1, -2],k = 7) == 0
    assert candidate(arr = [5, -1, 5],k = 1) == 9
    assert candidate(arr = [5, -1, 5],k = 3) == 27
    assert candidate(arr = [-5, 4, -1],k = 4) == 4
    assert candidate(arr = [10000, 10000, 10000],k = 50000) == 499999993
    assert candidate(arr = [2, -1, 2],k = 2) == 6
    assert candidate(arr = [0, 0, 0],k = 100) == 0
